name: post-list
description: Blog index composing a heading, a line of description and a list of post cards — picture, badge tag, linked title, clamped excerpt and an avatar byline — in a grid, with a featured first post, or as a single horizontal list, with an optional staggered entrance. Composition only: zero JavaScript, no controller, no reactive directives — the three layouts and the entrance are pure CSS.

heading.description: The section heading. Give it an id and point the section's aria-labelledby at it so the region is named

description.description: Supporting line under the heading, muted and capped at the content measure

items.description: The list of posts — a real <ul> so assistive tech announces the count

item.description: One list item, holding exactly one card

card.description: The post card, drawn by the pattern from the card aliases: an <article> named by its title through aria-labelledby, media over content, lifting on hover

media.description: A link to the post wrapping a plain with alt text; the alt is the link's name, so it describes the picture. The picture is cropped to 16:9 and leans in while the card is hovered or focused

content.description: The text column of the card, padded by --card-padding; holds tag, title, excerpt and meta

tag.description: Category line above the title, holding a nested data-ui='badge'

title.description: The post title in the heading voice, wrapping a nested data-ui='link' so the whole title is the link. Give it an id and point the card's aria-labelledby at it

excerpt.description: Muted summary clamped to --post-list-lines lines, so the cards in a row end on the same line

meta.description: Byline row pushed to the bottom of the content: a nested data-ui='avatar' data-size='sm', the author in a <span>, a <time datetime> and the reading time in a <span>. Text items are separated by a decorative middle dot

footer.description: Closing action row under the list — typically one 'View all posts' link as a nested data-ui='button'

animate.description: Stagger the items in: each one arrives --motion-stagger after the sibling before it, scrubbed by scroll where the browser has view timelines and played once on load where not. Twelve steps are counted; items past the twelfth arrive with it. Removed entirely under reduced motion and in print.

--post-list-gap.description: Gap between the cards, in both axes (custom property). Pass a spacing token.

--post-list-lines.description: How many lines the excerpt shows before it is clamped (custom property). An integer.

required_attrs: aria-labelledby on the section pointing at the heading id
aria-labelledby on each card pointing at its title id
alt text on every image inside a media link — the alt is the link's accessible name
descriptive link text in every title (never 'read more')
datetime on the <time> inside the meta part
a11y.notes: The section heading is an h2 and every post title an h3, so the index never skips a level. Each post exposes two links to the same destination — the picture and the title — which is the common index pattern; the picture link is named by its alt, so the two are distinguishable. The entrance animates opacity and translate only, is removed under prefers-reduced-motion and in print, and never removes a card from the accessibility tree.

keyboard.Tab: move through each card's picture link and title link in source order, then the footer action

templates.html:
{heading}

{description}

  • {post_tag}

    {post_title}

    {post_excerpt}

    {author_initials} {author} {date} {reading_time}
{footer_label}

notes: Nested primitives inside a slot keep their own five-attribute contract and must not carry a data-part: the badge sits inside [data-part="tag"], the link inside [data-part="title"], the avatar inside [data-part="meta"], the button inside [data-part="footer"].

The card is [data-part="card"], drawn by this pattern, not the card primitive: a post title belongs to the post rather than to a card header, and the pattern needs the picture and the content in a grid it can turn side by side. It reads the same --card-* aliases and the same --motion-hover-lift, so a theme that restyles cards restyles these.

The featured layout is the grid layout with the first item pulled out: from the md floor it spans the row and its card is media beside content. The list layout is one column at every width; from the sm floor each card is a 16rem picture beside the content. Below those floors both are the stacked phone card.

The entrance is the same choreography as a staggered reveal, read from the same motion tokens, so a theme that re-points --motion-reveal-* or --motion-stagger restyles this too. It is built in rather than composed because the stagger has to count the <li> children of the list, which a wrapping reveal cannot reach through the <ul>.
The excerpt clamp is the vendor box (-webkit-line-clamp); it is the one clamp every engine draws. Set --post-list-lines on the section, or on one item, to change the count.
